==College career== ===Freshman season=== Following the 2010 SEABL season, Bairstow moved to the United States to attend the [[University of New Mexico]]. In his freshman season, the young [[New Mexico Lobos men's basketball|Lobo squad]] was led by senior [[Dairese Gary]] and transfer [[Drew Gordon]] and finished the year 22–13 with an appearance in the [[2011 National Invitation Tournament|NIT]]. Bairstow was a member of one of the most accomplished freshman recruiting classes in Lobo history, along with [[Kendall Williams]], [[Tony Snell (basketball)|Tony Snell]] and [[Alex Kirk]].{{cite web |url=http://www.abqjournal.com/363401/sports/this-lobo-class-was-one-of-classiest-ever.html |title=This Lobo class was one of classiest ever |work=abqjournal.com |date=6 March 2014 |access-date=8 July 2014 |archive-date=20 July 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140720015753/http://www.abqjournal.com/363401/sports/this-lobo-class-was-one-of-classiest-ever.html |url-status=live }} He appeared in 31 games but played sparingly, averaging 2.6 points and 1.8 rebounds in 9.7 minutes per game.{{cite web |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/cameron-bairstow-1.html |title=Cameron Bairstow Stats |work=Sports-Reference.com |access-date=4 March 2014 |archive-date=25 March 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190325213910/https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/cameron-bairstow-1.html |url-status=live }} ===Sophomore season=== As a sophomore, Bairstow became a regular rotation player, appearing in 34 games, averaging 3.7 points and 3.6 rebounds in 15.4 minutes per game. Fellow Australian [[Hugh Greenwood]] joined the Lobos as a freshman in 2011–12 – he and Bairstow were teammates at the AIS in 2009 and 2010. Gordon had a dominating senior season, while Williams and Snell each averaged in double figures. The Lobos finished the season 28–7 after earning a share of the regular season [[Mountain West Conference]] (MWC) title, winning the conference tournament championship, and appearing in the [[2012 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]].{{cite web |last=Stevens |first=Richard |url=http://www.golobos.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=26000&ATCLID=209057479 |title=Stevens: New Mexico Lobos Men's Basketball 2011–12 Season Review |work=GoLobos.com |date=10 April 2012 |access-date=8 July 2014}} ===Junior season=== In Bairstow's junior season, 2012–13, the Lobos jumped out to a 12–0 start against a difficult schedule and climbed into the national rankings, later peaking at No. 10. The team's offence struggled at times, leading to a couple of blowout losses, and Bairstow was inserted into the starting line-up in late January. The Lobos then won nine of ten and clinched the regular season MWC title. Bairstow played in all 35 games and averaged 9.7 points and 5.9 rebounds in 24.1 minutes per game. His numbers climbed to 12 points and seven rebounds a game after he became a starter. Williams, Snell and Kirk all averaged in double figures. The Lobos won the MWC tournament championship, and Bairstow was named to the all-tournament team after averaging 13 points and 8.7 rebounds. The team suffered a disappointing upset to Harvard in the [[2013 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]], finishing the season 29–6, but Bairstow was one of the bright spots for the Lobos, tallying 15 points and 9 rebounds.New Mexico vs. Harvard, [https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=330800167 Boxscore], ESPN.com, 21 March 2013. ===Senior season=== Bairstow had a break-out season as a senior in 2013–14, recording one of the most remarkable improvements ever by a Lobo player. In 34 games, he averaged 20.4 points, 7.4 rebounds, 1.6 assists and 1.5 blocks per game, scoring 20 points or more in 21 games.New Mexico Athletics, [https://web.archive.org/web/20140429044526/https://admin.xosn.com/pdf9/2560546.pdf 2013–14 Lobo Men's Basketball Game Notes], p.68. The increase in his scoring average of 10.7 points was the third best in school history,Lobo Game Notes 2013–14, p.22. and he is the first Lobo player to average less than ten points one season and over twenty the next.{{cite web |last=Stevens |first=Richard |url=http://www.golobos.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=26000&ATCLID=209457987 |title=Stevens: UNM Lobos Men's Basketball 2013–14 Review |work=GoLobos.com |date=8 April 2014 |access-date=8 July 2014 |archive-date=29 April 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140429044908/http://www.golobos.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=26000&ATCLID=209457987 |url-status=dead }} The Lobos finished second in the MWC but won the conference tournament championship for the third straight season, and Bairstow was named tournament MVP. The team was again upset in the [[2014 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]], by Stanford, despite 24 points and eight rebounds by Bairstow. The Lobos completed the season 27–7, giving them a combined record of 106–33 during Bairstow's four years, making his the second-winningest class ever for the program.Lobo Game Notes 2013–14, p.19. Bairstow was named to the All-MWC first team after leading the conference in points scored, points per game, field goals made and attempted, field goal percentage, free throws made and attempted, and [[Player Efficiency Rating]]. He was honoured as a Second Team All-American by Sports Illustrated, Third Team All-American by NBC Sports and CBS Sports, and Honorable Mention All-American by the Associated Press. Bairstow gained attention during his senior season for his ritual of going to the weight room to lift after games, while still in uniform, receiving praise from opposing coaches and the media for his commitment and work ethic.{{cite web |last=Grammer |first=Geoff |url=http://www.abqjournal.com/301955/sports/neal-adjusting-to-grind-is-tough.html |title=Lobo basketball: Newcomers still adjusting to grind |work=abqjournal.com |date=16 November 2013 |access-date=8 July 2014 |archive-date=19 July 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140719202435/http://www.abqjournal.com/301955/sports/neal-adjusting-to-grind-is-tough.html |url-status=live }}{{cite web |last=Grammer |first=Geoff |url=http://www.abqjournal.com/421270/sports/bairstow-drafted-by-the-chicago-bulls.html |title=UNM's Bairstow drafted by the Chicago Bulls |work=abqjournal.com |date=26 June 2014 |access-date=8 July 2014 |archive-date=2 July 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140702215758/http://www.abqjournal.com/421270/sports/bairstow-drafted-by-the-chicago-bulls.html |url-status=live }} When he arrived at New Mexico, he measured 6–8 and 210 pounds; by his senior season he was listed as 6–9 and 250 pounds; at the [[NBA Draft Combine]] in May 2014, he surprised observers by measuring just under 6–10, suggesting he had still been growing.{{cite web |last=Grammer |first=Geoff |url=http://www.abqjournal.com/415835/sports/bairstow-untroubled-by-doubters.html |title=Ex-Lobo Bairstow keeps expanding his game as NBA draft approaches |work=abqjournal.com |date=15 June 2014 |access-date=8 July 2014 |archive-date=10 July 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140710002952/http://www.abqjournal.com/415835/sports/bairstow-untroubled-by-doubters.html |url-status=live }}{{cite web |url=http://www.nbadraft.net/players/cameron-bairstow |title=41 – Cameron Bairstow |work=NBADraft.net |access-date=8 July 2014 |archive-date=30 June 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140630031120/http://www.nbadraft.net/players/cameron-bairstow |url-status=live }} Bairstow was arguably the most improved player in the history of the Lobo program. Head coach [[Craig Neal]] stated, "I don't think there's anybody who's come farther in four years. I don't think there's anybody who could have predicted what he's done this season."{{cite web |last=Grammer |first=Geoff |url=http://www.abqjournal.com/362867/sports/aussie-transformed-into-goto-scorer.html |title=Cameron Bairstow: Aussie transformed into go-to scorer |work=abqjournal.com |date=5 March 2014 |access-date=8 July 2014 |archive-date=19 July 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140719200118/http://www.abqjournal.com/362867/sports/aussie-transformed-into-goto-scorer.html |url-status=live }} After his success in international play during the summer of 2013, Bairstow received offers to play professionally, but he chose to return for his senior season and complete his degree. He was honoured by the MWC as academic all-conference as a senior and earned a degree in Exercise Science at UNM; he aspires to study physiotherapy after his playing career has ended.{{cite web |url-status=live }} as well as the first two games of the regular season. In his NBL debut on 16 October, Bairstow recorded 15 points, seven rebounds and three assists off the bench in a 96–93 overtime loss to the [[Adelaide 36ers]].{{cite web |url=http://www.nbl.com.au/featured-news/randle-gutsy-sixers-overthrow-bairstow-debut-ot/ |title=Randle, gutsy Sixers overthrow Bairstow debut in OT |work=NBL.com.au |date=16 October 2016 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161019080334/http://www.nbl.com.au/featured-news/randle-gutsy-sixers-overthrow-bairstow-debut-ot/ |archive-date=19 October 2016}}{{cite web |url=https://www.fibalivestats.com/u/NBL/314701/bs.html |title=Bullets vs 36ers |date=16 October 2016 |work=FIBALiveStats.com |access-date=16 October 2016 |archive-date=17 May 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180517082131/http://www.fibalivestats.com/u/NBL/314701/bs.html |url-status=live }} On 20 December, he was ruled out for the rest of the season after scans revealed an [[anterior cruciate ligament]] injury to his left knee. He suffered the injury during overtime in Brisbane's 91–85 loss to the [[Illawarra Hawks]] the previous night.{{cite web |url=http://www.foxsports.com.au/basketball/nbl/brisbane-bullets-bigman-cameron-bairstow-to-miss-remainder-of-nbl-season-with-acl-injury/news-story/6e5dc4a166322aff4fcbd485ecdb5eda |title=Brisbane Bullets big-man Cameron Bairstow to miss remainder of NBL season with ACL injury |date=20 December 2016 |work=FoxSports.com.au |access-date=20 December 2016 |archive-date=22 December 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161222165906/http://www.foxsports.com.au/basketball/nbl/brisbane-bullets-bigman-cameron-bairstow-to-miss-remainder-of-nbl-season-with-acl-injury/news-story/6e5dc4a166322aff4fcbd485ecdb5eda |url-status=live }} Having never previously suffered a serious injury, Bairstow had now copped two in the space of six months, including a career-threatening knee injury.{{cite web |url=http://www.nbl.com.au/news/article/cam-bairstow-a-force-again-in-bullets-finals-push-2 |title=Bairstow a Force Again in Bullets Finals' Push |date=2 February 2019 |work=NBL.com.au |access-date=2 February 2019 |archive-date=2 February 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190202212333/http://www.nbl.com.au/news/article/cam-bairstow-a-force-again-in-bullets-finals-push-2 |url-status=live }} In 13 games over the first two months of the 2016–17 season, he averaged 12.8 points and 6.5 rebounds per game. After missing the entire 2017–18 season with the injury,{{cite web |last=Davis |first=Greg |url=http://www.couriermail.com.au/sport/brisbane-bullets-rocked-cameron-bairstow-injury/news-story/1063196022f33feeaffc5199e94458bd |title=Brisbane Bullets rocked Cameron Bairstow injury |date=3 June 2017 |work=CourierMail.com.au |access-date=6 June 2017 |archive-date=7 June 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170607062338/http://www.couriermail.com.au/sport/brisbane-bullets-rocked-cameron-bairstow-injury/news-story/1063196022f33feeaffc5199e94458bd |url-status=live }} Bairstow re-signed with the Bullets on a two-year deal on 4 May 2018.{{cite web |url=http://www.nbl.com.au/news/article/41804-cam-bairstow-returns-to-the-brisbane-bullets |title=Cam Bairstow returns to the Brisbane Bullets |date=4 May 2018 |work=NBL.com.au |access-date=4 May 2018 |archive-date=4 May 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180504225555/http://www.nbl.com.au/news/article/41804-cam-bairstow-returns-to-the-brisbane-bullets |url-status=live }} He returned to action in the 2018–19 season. In conjunction with the camp, Bairstow coordinated a Lobo alumni all-star game, along with Brandon Mason, a former [[New Mexico State Aggies men's basketball|New Mexico State Aggie]] player and later a Lobo assistant coach.{{cite web |last=Grammer |first=Geoff |url=http://www.abqjournal.com/635750/mason-returning-to-aggie-roots-joins-nmsu-hoops-staff.html |title=Mason returning to Aggie roots, joins NMSU hoops staff |work=abqjournal.com |date=28 August 2015 |access-date=22 July 2016 |archive-date=30 November 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161130132919/https://www.abqjournal.com/635750/mason-returning-to-aggie-roots-joins-nmsu-hoops-staff.html |url-status=live }} Twenty-one former Lobo players took part in the game, including NBA veterans [[Danny Granger]] and [[Tony Snell (basketball)|Tony Snell]], drawing an attendance of 9,497 fans at The Pit for an entertaining exhibition.{{cite web |last=Grammer |first=Geoff |url=http://www.abqjournal.com/605757/once-a-lobo.html |title=Former Lobos romp in the Pit |work=abqjournal.com |date=29 June 2015 |access-date=22 July 2016}} The event included a slam-dunk contest, autograph session for fans, and an auction of Lobo memorabilia.
